status: authored 2026-10-11, generator tools/scar_tarn.py; the tarn and its own wood were applied to staging 2026-10-11 (docs/STATE.md), growth.arms (2026-10-12) is in the repository only. NOT in the live world. The recess is measured on the canonical heightmap, which the live world predates (docs/STATE.md 'Pads in the world': the Scar's pad is in the heightmap and in staging only), so this waits for the live re-export like the Scar itself.
owner: 2026-10-11: "I like the Scar thematically, but I think we need something or an environment inhabiting the area now. It feels weird to see the big mountain completely empty. I thought the north-west side of the mountain has a cool recessed point, where some water could make for a pond, and we can plop some trees and alpha mons down to have taken over the afflicted area of the Scar or something."

place.reading: Where the mountain turns its back on the dead city: a closed bowl on the north-north-west shoulder of Mt Vessu, about 95 blocks north of the Scar's north cliff (the old avenue ends at z806) and 43 blocks below its pad (y280), holding a tarn that no one dug. Spruce and birch have come down into it from the ridges and stand thickest at the water; the ground under them is moss and podzol where the Scar's is bare stone and snow; a few terrace walls the same bricks as the Scar's lie half under the moss. It is not tended and it is not empty: the things that live here are bigger than the things on the slopes around it. Optional, off every route (Route 3 is 769 blocks away, Route 4 688), reached by walking down the mountain's north face from the Scar.
place.story_note: Nothing here is canon beyond the owner's line (the afflicted ground taken over by nature and alphas). The brick stubs are the Scar's own palette (data/placements.json settlements.the_scar streets: cracked_stone_bricks, mossy_stone_bricks); they say 'the city reached this far' without naming why.
place.dark_by_design: No lamps and no lanterns, like the Scar (docs/STATE.md 'Places are lit as towns': the Scar is dark by design).

measured.how: tools/scar_tarn.py report, from tools/ground.py (the canonical heightmap, rounded); a priority-flood fill of 1700..2500 x 550..1300 with the window's edge open found two closed hollows >= 2 deep over 40 columns on the massif: this one (2204 columns at fill level y239, max fill depth 11) and a larger one to the north-east at x2154..2354 z648..793 (14,903 columns, fill level y223, depth 30) that is NOT the north-west recess
measured.summit: Mt Vessu's summit is (1864, 760) y300; the Scar pad is y280 at (2110, 950); the hollow is NNW of the pad, 237 blocks north of its centre

pond.water_level_why: the top water block. The hollow's own spill is y239 (the lowest rim column); 237 leaves two blocks of natural freeboard at the lowest point of the rim and the generator lifts any rim column below 238 to 238, so a column that the world holds one block under the heightmap (tools/ground.py: 'one block low at water edges', 0.15%) still holds the water
pond.lobe_seeds_why: the hollow's two dips (ground y228 at x1988 z727 and y229 at x2017 z707); a Habitat Block stands in the bed of each so both halves of the tarn hold an alpha

arms.why: The owner, 2026-10-12, looking at the tarn on the map: "The forest should expand toward the Scar, maybe envelop some of it, and then down the back and side of the mountain." The wood above (water-centred, radius 48) is LAYER 1 and is left byte for byte as it was, so a re-apply over the wood already in staging adds to it and moves nothing. The arms are LAYER 2: tongues of the same wood (the same kinds, shares, heights, ground cover and plants as the keys above) laid along spines read off the heightmap. Each arm is its own function (cobblers:scar_tarn/arm_<id>), held in its own forceload by step R9ST.
arms.max_relief_why: a trunk stands only where the 3x3 around it varies by two blocks or less (a 45 degree slope along an axis, about 35 on a diagonal); the tarn's own wood allows three. The red bands on the map (the hollow's north wall, the west wall under Thundurus's shoulder, the pad's feather) have none, so the wood thins and stops at them: it climbs by the gentle spurs and does not cross the cliffs
arms.inside_landmark_why: every written column is inside the Mt Vessu outline (data/landmarks.json) so the wood is the mountain's and does not run out onto Tri-Peaks or the lowland; the 24-block authored clearance from that outline (a line the audit sweeps) keeps it that far inside

keep_clear_core.why: the city's core, so it stays readable: the convex hull of the rectangles the house lots fill along the cross road, the north road and the south road (data/placements.json settlements.the_scar.plan: half the road's width + setback 2 + lot depth 11 each side, one lot + gap past each end) grown by 3. The 24-block clearance from every street line already keeps the wood out of the lots; this closes the two chamfered corners of the hull (north-west and north-east) that no street line reaches

arms.paint_gain_why: the ground cover's probability is the tree probability times this, capped at 0.92: moss and podzol thin out with the trees

avoid_boxes.why: Thundurus's sealed chamber (data/legendaries.json thundurus: portal (1888, 822), plug_depth 6, approach bearing 180 passage 12, chamber 19 x 19, spawn_free_zone [1872, 816, 1904, 856]): the spawn-free box plus 24 on every side. Nothing is grown on the plug, over the shaft or on the walk-up to it

lobes.why: TOWARD THE SCAR, west half: from the tarn's south shore over the gentle ramp (y240 to 280) onto the pad's north apron, then round the pad's west rim. The pad is the Scar's own ground (y280, pressed flat, radius 150 round (2110, 950)); this is its outskirts, the ground the city stopped at, and it envelops the city's north-west corner from the avenue's end round to the cross road's west end. The field is drawn wide on purpose, over the whole north-west quadrant of the disc, and the keep-clear net (24 from every authored x/z and line, the avoid boxes) carves the city and Thundurus's plug out of it: the wood ends at the ruins' edge (the lots reach 16 from a road) and leaves the streets, the plaza and the houses readable

TOWARD THE SCAR, east half: along the pad's north apron east of the old avenue, thinning toward the north-east rim; the avenue's own approach (24 either side of x2110) stays open so the road still ends at the cliff in clear air

DOWN THE BACK: Mt Vessu's north face, the slope that turns its back on the Scar. The hollow's north wall (z636 to 700, red on the relief map) is bare cliff; under it the face is a gentle slope (20 to 30 degrees) that falls to the Mt Vessu outline at z556 to 600, and the 24-block authored clearance from that outline leaves a band about 50 deep (z584 to 634). The wood spills over the wall at its low points and runs down into that band. West half, under the tarn
DOWN THE BACK, east half: the same band under the tarn's east end and along the gap between the hollow wall and the north-east ring

DOWN THE SIDE: the east flank, where the pad's feather falls away east of the Scar, 25 to 30 degrees down to the outline at x2384 to 2396. Read off the heightmap: the other flank is not available. West of the pad the mountain drops 100 blocks in 50 (x1830 to 1880, y217 to 291, the wall under Thundurus's shoulder) and inside the outline's 24-block margin there is no gentle ground between that wall and the outline at x1792 to 1820, so the side the wood can reach is the east. It continues the north-east arm round the pad's rim and down

land.place: the tarn's north-east bank, in the spruce
the tarn's south-west bank, in the birch

water.place: the bed of the tarn's west dip
the bed of the tarn's east dip

wards.settings_why: the Ursaluna den's and the elder nests' settings (data/habitat_blocks.json ursaluna_den_outskirts_ward: spawn_range 16, chance 1.0, TICK, cancel_range -1), unchanged because nothing measured says another value is better; max_spawns 2 per grove ward and 1 per water ward = at most 6 alphas alive at once. Activated blocks refill as an alpha is beaten or caught, which makes the tarn a repeatable alpha-gem source (data/alpha_spoils.json): the owner's call whether that is wanted

alphas.band_why: Mt Vessu's table is 22-28 at tier 3 (data/spawns.json subregions mt_vessu level_band) and tier 3's next cap is 35 (data/encounter_design.json rules.hearts.next_cap['3']): an alpha band of 29-33 is one above the table's top and two under the next cap, the Wardenhold Froslass precedent (a place's one boss-strength creature, above its band, under the next cap). IN GAME the number is not what a player fights: the jar's cobblemon:alpha_level_matching sensor re-levels a wild alpha within 32 blocks of a player to their highest party level +8 (party 21-30) or +12 (31-45), at least the level it evolves at (data/encounter_design.json rules.hearts.alpha_level_matching, read from bytecode and not seen in game)
alphas.how: an ACTIVATED Habitat Block keeps up to max_spawns of its pool alive; the pool entry's `modifiers` is a PokemonProperties the jar copies into the spawn detail (HabitatSpawn.createSpawnDetail: modifiers.copy(), setSpecies, PokemonSpawnDetail.setPokemon, read from the 1.8.0 jar's bytecode 2026-10-11) and PokemonProperties.commonApply calls Pokemon.setAlpha(true) when isAlpha is set, the same property the jar's own alpha spawns use ('fearow ... alpha=true'). NOT seen in game; the proof is EXP-066's alpha spoils on one of these

entries.why: Wooper evolves to Quagsire at 20, under the band; the slow brown water-dweller that would own a still tarn (it spawns submerged in marsh_creek already)
Chinchou evolves to Lanturn at 27, under the band; the glow in a place with no lamps
Magikarp evolves to Gyarados at 20, under the band; the one that has driven everything else out of the water
Rockruff evolves to Lycanroc at 25, under the band; a rock wolf on a mountain, and the one species of the three that already ranges Route 3 and 4 (mt_clay), the pack leader of a scarred slope
Gible evolves to Gabite at 24, under the band (Garchomp is 48); a mountain dragon that nests in a hollow, the cave/mountain dragon family (no Gible line in any Vessu roster)

Gastly evolves to Haunter at 25, under the band (Gengar is a trade); the dead city's ghost, drawn to the ruins at the bank. Ghost types fit any country, which is why it is the one that is here because of the Scar

blocks.why: every block the generator may write; it refuses any other. Water is the only spawn-condition block (data/spawn_blocks.json) and is whitelisted for 'scar_tarn' in data/spawn_block_policy.json. No concrete (contract C4), no leaves or flowers that a spawn condition names (oak and dark oak leaves, flowering azalea, lily pad and seagrass are why they are not used)

rules.authored_clearance_why: no written column nearer than this to an x/z another data file authors (the mt_vessu landmark outline's corners at (2154, 682) and (1940, 600) are 35 and 80+ away)

authored_box_exempt.why: the Scar's town footprint, a 300 x 300 planning square round the pad (data/towns.json the_scar). The arms grow in its outskirts on purpose (the owner, 2026-10-12: envelop some of it), so the 'a box holds no written column' sweep is replaced for it by the audit's own Scar rules: nothing within 24 of a street line (the generic line sweep, unchanged), nothing in a ruin's footprint or the plaza, and no trunk in the city's lot bands or core. Its nine 3 x 3 points and every other authored point and line keep the 24-block clearance
